title: Stream window alignment and aggregate cadence fix for console cohort charts
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Symptoms observed: multiple customers reported transient spikes in per-model and per-customer cohort charts in the Console after hitting short rate-limit bursts or during aggressive streaming workloads. Investigations show duplicated rows in minute-level aggregates and small time-shifts between rate-limit ingress events and downstream aggregation windows. The dashboards intermittently show 2–6x token counts for 30–90s slices after bursts. This ticket unifies the temporal bucketing and fixes deduplication paths so console cohort charts reflect canonical billing windows and remove duplicate attribution from retries and streaming flushes.
root_cause_analysis: Two independent issues combined to create visible chart inaccuracies: 1) ingestion services stamp events with arrival_time while the aggregation pipeline buckets events by event_time floored to the minute; retries and request bursts sometimes land across boundary conditions causing the same logical request to be counted in adjacent minute buckets. 2) streaming vs non-streaming instrumentations used different id heuristics: streaming flush events and final response events lacked a shared canonical dedupe key, so the same token sequences could be counted twice when the streaming consumer later emitted completion events. Together these produced short-lived spikes that show up in cohort and per-model breakdowns.
proposed_solution: 1) Add a canonical billing_window_id at the ingestion edge computed as floor_to_minute(request_start_utc) and propagate it downstream as the single join key for all usage rollups. 2) Introduce canonical_event_id = concat(request_id, '-', tentative_sequence_id) and enforce deduplication in both streaming and batch consumers based on this id. 3) Update aggregation SQL/jobs to join on billing_window_id instead of event_time buckets. 4) Run a targeted backfill job to recompute aggregates for the prior 72 hours into a separate topic 'golden_usage_v2' and switch dashboards to read from golden_usage_v2 once validated. 5) Add monitoring dashboards and reconciliation alerts comparing golden_usage_v2 against raw logs with a 0.5% tolerance.
acceptance_criteria: Console cohort charts no longer show >5% transient spikes related to bursty rate-limit events in canary orgs
Backfill run produces golden_usage_v2 and discrepancies vs raw logs <0.5% for token counts across sample customers
No increase in infer/runtime tail latency or aggregator latency beyond current SLAs
Change passes security review checklist for ingest metadata propagation
work_items: ingest: compute and attach billing_window_id at edge (ingest-proxy) — implement + unit tests
streaming-consumer: add canonical_event_id dedupe path and idempotent writes to usage topic
batch-aggregator: switch group-by key to billing_window_id and update retention semantics
backfill-job: Spark job to recompute last 72h into golden_usage_v2 topic with partitioning by customer and model
console: add feature flag to switch cohort charts to golden_usage_v2 and a diff-view to compare old vs new series
observability: reconciliation dashboard and alert for >0.5% divergence (sampled customers)
testing_plan: Run unit tests and property-based tests for bucketing behaviour. Deploy changes to staging and run the synthetic burst harness that replays production burst traces (script located in scripts/burst-replay). Validate that aggregator output for replay matches golden reference within 0.1%. Canary rollout to 5 small customer orgs for 48 hours, monitor reconciliation metrics and dashboard diffs before full switch. Backfill job dry-run against sample partitions before full run.
rollback_plan: Keep old aggregates topic (golden_usage_v1) untouched. Console will read from feature-flagged golden_usage_v2; if divergence or regressions appear, flip feature flag back to v1 and notify stakeholders. Backfill writes to a separate topic so it is safe to abort and truncate without user-visible impact.
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: backfill job could overwhelm Kafka or storage. Mitigation: run backfill with rate-limited producers and partition-aware parallelism; monitor lag and throttle. Risk: slight delay in dashboard propagation during canary. Mitigation: notify SRE and schedule canary during low-traffic windows and add automated rollback if reconciliation fails.
